prompt.context: Your client 'Impact Consulting' is an industry leader in Technology consulting globally. Over the last 3 years, Impact Consulting has grown its customer base but overall profitability has reduced. The CFO has hired us to determine what factors are driving low profitability. Impact Consulting is a multinational company with offices primarily in the US and UK. It provides consulting and implementation services in Cloud Products (e.g., Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, Google Cloud), Customer Relationship Management Products, and Enterprise Productivity Products (e.g., Office 365). Revenue has been stagnant over the last 3 years.
prompt.question: What factors are driving low profitability at Impact Consulting?

clarifying_info.q: What is the number of working days in a year?
What is the number of working hours in a day?
Will revenue or billing hours change this year?
clarifying_info.a: Assume revenue will not change this year and the number of billing hours will remain the same

clarifying_info.q: What are the average salaries for employees in low cost countries?

exhibits.title: Impact Consulting Organization Chart
exhibits.shows: Organization chart of billable employees broken down by role, showing headcount, average salary, and hours billed
exhibits.data: Consultants: Count=600, Avg. Salary=$140K (includes base + fringe), Hours Billed=742K; Project Leads: Count=200, Avg. Salary=$180K, Hours Billed=210K; Partners: Count=40, Avg. Salary=$220K, Hours Billed=46K; Non-Billable Employees also noted

exhibits.title: Average Annual Billability Trends
exhibits.shows: Bar chart comparing Impact Consulting's average billability % versus Industry Average % for Consultants, Project Leads, and Partners
exhibits.data: Consultant: Impact Consulting=60%, Industry Avg=80%; Project Lead: Impact Consulting=65%, Industry Avg=80%; Partner: Impact Consulting=70%, Industry Avg=60%; (chart y-axis range 0-80, x-axis shows three roles)

framework: Internal - Cost: Employee salary, travel, perks, severance, training, health/medical benefits
Internal - Pricing: High discounts, low billing rates compared to market
Internal - Product: Lack of IP in custom solutions, changing B2B product versions driving high training/talent costs
Internal - Delivery: Underestimated effort, mix of Fixed vs. T&M projects, inappropriate staffing, quality issues leading to free rework
Internal - Organizational Factors: Labor pyramid, work location (high vs. low cost country), deep hierarchy causing delays, sales & marketing effectiveness, lack of talent
External - Competition: High competition reducing billing rates and raising quality expectations
External - Nature of Engagements: Low ticket-size engagements, clients increasingly building own IT teams causing coordination delays

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1 (org chart and billability data), what is the potential cost savings in $M from workforce reduction if Impact Consulting meets industry billability standards?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Consultants and Project Leads are below industry standard (60% and 65% vs. 80%), while Partners are above industry standard (70% vs. 60%) and should not be reduced. Candidate should ask for working days and hours per day, then compute hours available per employee at 80% billability, derive headcount needed to cover existing billed hours, and calculate savings from the reduction. A strong candidate also flags risks of downsizing (business impact, timeline, retraining to raise billability).

math.setup: Target billability = 80%. Total hours available per employee = 80% x 220 days x 8 hrs = 1,408 hrs (~1,400). Use current billed hours to calculate required headcount.
steps: Hours available per employee at 80% billability = 0.80 x 220 x 8 = 1,408 hrs
math.answer: $18.8M in potential cost savings from workforce reduction

questions.prompt: Currently all employees are based in high-cost countries (US, UK). How much additional cost savings in $M can be achieved if 20% of the (reduced) consultants and project leaders are shifted to a Low Cost Center (LCC)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the 20% shift to the already-reduced headcount (530 consultants, 150 PLs), not the original headcount. Multiply the number shifted by the salary differential between high-cost and low-cost countries.

math.setup: Use reduced headcounts: 530 Consultants, 150 Project Leads. LCC salaries: Consultants $60K, Project Leads $90K. Shift 20% of each to LCC.
math.answer: $11.18M in additional cost savings from shifting 20% of reduced workforce to low-cost centers

brainstorming.prompt: Low repeat customer rate has been an issue for Impact Consulting over the last two years. What are some factors that you think are causing this problem?

categories.name: Quality of Work
ideas: Low quality of work in past engagements
Poor quality of talent on engagements

categories.name: Changing Customer Needs
ideas: Customers need consulting in newer products that Impact does not cover
Clients are investing in and building their own IT departments
Clients expect lower prices or higher discounts than Impact can offer

categories.name: Other Factors
ideas: Increased competition, including big companies like Microsoft offering their own IT consulting for their products
Lack of senior-level relationships at client organizations

recommendation: Impact Consulting should increase the billability of Consultants and Project Leads to match the industry standard of 80%, which will allow a workforce reduction saving approximately $18.8M
Impact Consulting should migrate 20% of the reduced consultant and project lead workforce to low-cost countries, generating an additional $11.18M in savings
risks: Reducing workforce must not disrupt existing client engagements; the reduction should be phased carefully
Retraining and performance management should be explored to help current employees become more billable before resorting to layoffs
next_steps: Identify low-cost countries with adequate talent pools for Technology consulting
Establish or expand offices in those low-cost locations
Develop a phased workforce transition and retraining plan
